meta.description: Priya Vishwanathan: thirty-five years with IHCL; she helped build and scale amã Stays & Trails. Advisory for homestay and hotel owners, growing groups and boards, and conversations on service and leadership.

sections.name: Priya <t>Vishwanathan</t>
sections.sub: I helped build and scale amã Stays & Trails. <t>Thirty-five years with IHCL.</t>
sections.note: अतिथि देवो भव · the guest is god

sections.label: Where I built my career

items.k: Senior Assessor, Tata Business Excellence Model

sections.src: Logos belong to their owners and appear here only to show where I have worked.

items.k: A homestay brand, built and scaled.
items.t: The most fulfilling chapter of my thirty-five years with IHCL: helping build and scale amã Stays & Trails into a distinctive hospitality brand. As General Manager I held the P&L, the owners and the guests, across India.
items.d: From nine bungalows at launch to 370+ today. IHCL figures.

items.k: From isolated hotels to one organisation.
items.t: Fifteen years in Business Excellence, part of the work that moved IHCL from hotels run in isolation to one organisation with structured standards. Senior Assessor of the Tata Business Excellence Model.
items.d: Customer-satisfaction work across more than 100 hotels.

items.t: I joined IHCL in 1990 from IHM Pusa: St. James’ Court in London, the Taj Mahal in New Delhi, then eight years as Regional Manager for Karnataka.
items.d: Front office, club floors, quality and operations.

sections.label: The most fulfilling chapter
sections.title: amã Stays <t>& Trails.</t>
sections.body: Families came to us with houses their parents had left them. We listened to the owners, kept what made each house itself, and built a brand around it.

img.alt: A planter’s bungalow veranda at dawn (illustrative)

sections.lead: Something I wrote down before a conversation on Inspire Someone Today:
sections.q: “Success is not measured by how many people know your name. It is measured by how many people are better because they crossed your path.”

sections.label: In conversation
sections.title: Hear it <t>in my words.</t>
sections.lede: Two long conversations recorded in 2026: one with a hotelier, one about a life in hospitality.

items.t: Hotels Are Solving the Wrong Problem
items.d: Data over instinct, improvement without overspending, Business Excellence at IHCL, and why a struggling culture is easier to fix than a struggling business.

items.t: How Many People Are Better Because They Crossed Your Path?
items.d: Day three at the Taj, homestays built with the families who own them, service without servility, and leaving at the top.

items.q: “Every time a guest has complained and been not so polite to me, it was a learning: what we had to correct and what we did wrong.”
“If you have to respect others, you’ve got to first respect yourself.”

items.t: Good to great touches the heart.
items.q: “I was in a business, not in a charity. Good to great really happens when you do something that touches somebody’s heart.”

sections.label: Career
sections.quote: From a duty manager’s desk <t>to a national brand.</t>
sections.sub: Thirty-five years with IHCL, ending in its most fulfilling chapter: helping build and scale amã Stays & Trails into a distinctive hospitality brand.

sections.label: Advisory
sections.sub: “Advising, mentoring and helping hospitality businesses build for the future.” The work I took up after IHCL.

sections.label: Today
sections.sub: Board Advisor and Principal Consultant at HOSPI Sigma. Regional jury (South), BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Awards 2026. National Vice President, WICCI Diversity & Inclusion Council.
